traceability.notes:
The implementation for story docs/stories/010.3-DEV-MIGRATE-TO-IMPLEMENTS.story.md is close but does not fully meet the specified requirements and acceptance criteria.
What is implemented correctly: - A new ESLint rule `prefer-implements-annotation` exists and is linked to this story. - When enabled, it detects legacy `@story` + `@req` combinations and emits a `preferImplements` recommendation (REQ-OPTIONAL-WARNING). - It provides an auto-fix that converts simple single-story blocks (one @story path, one @story line, one or more simple @req lines) into a single `@implements` line, preserving indentation and comment structure (REQ-AUTO-FIX, REQ-SINGLE-STORY-FIX, REQ-PRESERVE-FORMAT, REQ-VALID-OUTPUT). - It detects mixed `@story`/`@req` + `@implements` and multi-story cases, emitting appropriate diagnostic messages without attempting unsafe fixes (REQ-MULTI-STORY-DETECT). - It does not alter the existing validation rules; when this rule is disabled, legacy @story/@req annotations continue to behave as before (REQ-BACKWARD-COMP-VALIDATION, Both Formats Valid). - Tests and documentation specific to this rule and story exist and pass.
Where it fails the story requirements: 1) Default enforcement level is wrong: - The story explicitly requires that the rule be **disabled by default** (default "off") to preserve backward compatibility for Release 0.1, with later phases possibly enabling it by default. - However, the plugin’s own `recommended` and `strict` configs set `"traceability/prefer-implements-annotation": "warn"` by default via TRACEABILITY_RULE_SEVERITIES. - This means that any user adopting the plugin’s recommended config will have migration warnings active immediately, contradicting the story’s requirement that the rule start life as opt-in and off by default. - While users can manually configure the rule off/warn/error, the exported default behavior does not match the story’s “default off” acceptance criterion (REQ-CONFIG-SEVERITY).
2) '@req without matching @story' is not warned on: - The Implementation Notes specifically call out the edge case "@req without matching @story (warn, cannot auto-fix)" as something the rule should handle. - In the current implementation, processComment returns early when `!hasStory || !hasReq`, so comments containing only @req (no @story) are entirely ignored – no warning, no cannot-auto-fix message. - The tests confirm and enshrine this behavior: "[REQ-BACKWARD-COMP-VALIDATION] comment with only @req is ignored" is a valid (no-error) test case. - Therefore, this part of REQ-MULTI-STORY-DETECT and the associated acceptance criteria is not met; the specified warning for '@req without matching @story' is missing.
Because of these two discrepancies – incorrect default severity (not off) and missing warning behavior for '@req without matching @story' – not all acceptance criteria and detailed requirements in the story are satisfied. The correct assessment for this story is FAILED.
